newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares down 1.74 percent in thin volume.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares down 1.74 percent in thin volume.

text.p: Istanbul shares fell in thin volume on Thursday when the index fluctuated in a band between 1,905 and 1,953.
The IMKB National-100 ended down 34 points, or 1.74 percent at 1,919.
Daily volume shrank to 17.58 trillion lira ($111.6 million), compared to Tuesday's 19.86 trillion lira ($ 127 million).

"The Bourse is squeezed under the pressure of rising interest rates and the US dollar. The domestic banks with long dollar positions may try to close their positions and that may create new domestic demand on the dollar. The Central Bank has to control the dollar carefully," said Vedat Konyali from Toprak Securities.
Daily trade volume was at its lowest level since June 19th, for more than a month.

"I guess the large portfolios shall wait for the next treasury auction which would be held on probably next week, before entering into new long positions at stocks," said Hakan Aksoy from Alfa Securities.

Of the 248 shares traded, losers outdid gainers by 175 to 40, and 33 remained unchanged. The IMKB Industrial lost 2.40 percent to 1,870, the IMKB Services dropped 1.48 percent to 1,860 and the IMKB Financial eased 1.01 percent to 2,065.
The index representing the electrical sector was the leading loser with 3.69 percent while the index of forest products lost 3.45 percent.

The most active share of the day was largely state-owned Turkish Airlines making alone 9.6 percent of the total volume, Is Bank's C group shares were up 2,000 to 60,000 and largely state owned giant flat steel producer Eregli was down 750 lira to 23,500.
The three made up 19.3 percent of the total volume.
